header.headline: Develop with us in the open
header.subhead: The landing site is public. Clinical content, locales, accessibility, and documentation contributions are reviewed like code.

tone: Star the repo if it helps. Watch for releases. Open an issue or ship a branch — we review.

ctas.label: Star the repo
ctas.body: If the direction is relevant to your work, a star helps others find it.

ctas.label: Watch for releases
ctas.body: Release notes ship with every content and design update.

ctas.label: Fork and adapt
ctas.body: Dual-licensed MIT / Apache-2.0. Fork it for your own landing work.

ctas.label: Open an issue
ctas.body: Bugs, content errors, status-label inconsistencies, and feature requests.

ctas.label: Ship a branch
ctas.body: Pull requests are reviewed. Include rationale and, for clinical content, sources.

goodFirstIssues.title: Good first issues
goodFirstIssues.note: Themes we keep open for new contributors.

items.title: Add a locale
items.body: The planned set is TR / EN / DE (roadmap). Help wire a new language into `_content/` and nav/footer labels.

items.title: Improve animation
items.body: Refine section transitions for the clinical-noir-teal design while respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`.

items.title: Fix SEO
items.body: Metadata, Open Graph tags, sitemap entries, and structured data for the landing pages.

items.title: Write a case study
items.body: Draft a clinical workflow narrative. Any number needs methodology + source + date + status; qualitative claims stay qualitative.

codeOfConduct.title: Code of conduct
codeOfConduct.body: Be precise, be respectful, cite sources. Clinical claims require sources; anecdote is not evidence. Harassment, bad-faith edits, and unverified medical claims in published content are not acceptable. Reports go to the maintainers via the repository's contact channel and are handled privately.

contributionRules: Every number needs methodology + source + date + status (see METRICS_POLICY.md).
"Designed for" never becomes "certified" in copy; architecture stays architecture.
No patient data, no real case data, no unattributed clinical guidance in issues or PRs.
